newsitem.title: USA: US jobs data showing some wage acceleration--Hamel.
newsitem.headline: US jobs data showing some wage acceleration--Hamel.

text.p: U.S. Department of Labor economist Harvey Hamel said Friday the latest jobs data are showing some signs of wage gains accelerating.

A May increase in earnings was in line with increases throughout 1997, with an average growth of about 3.7 percent to 3.8 percent over a year earlier, Hamel told Reuters Financial Television. That compares to last year's average of 3.0 percent to 3.3 percent, he said.

"Clearly there's been some wage acceleration," Hamel said. "There is no question about that. But on the other hand it has been pretty consistent through the first half of the year, at least through May."
Hamel said the annual adjustment to the jobs data was "very small" and did not have a major impact on the May data.
"I don't think the technical things we did to the surveys this month really caused much of an impact on what happened," he said.

The Labor Department reported that the unemployment rate edged down to 4.8 percent in May -- its lowest level since October 1973 -- from 4.9 percent in April. Payrolls rose by just 138,000 last month after increasing by a whopping 323,000 in April. The department had originally reported that payrolls grew by 142,000 in April.
Hamel said the adjustment in April was higher than usual, but noted that if April and May are averaged, additions to payroll were in line with recent trends.
